q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a conveyor belt per metre?
title: Conveyor belt carbon footprint per metre
short: Weigh the rubber covers and fabric or steel cord per metre and multiply by supplier figures. Add calendering, building and press curing energy, then divide the plant's energy by metres of belt dispatched, stated by width and ply.
audience: Rubber conveyor belt makers and mining and cement buyers

ul: Rubber compound for top and bottom covers.
EP fabric plies or steel cords.
Hydraulic curing presses heated by steam or thermic oil.

p: Report per metre with width, number of plies and cover thickness, the figures a buyer's tender already names.

example.title: Worked example: conveyor belt unit per metre (one month)
lines: Plant total: 101,000 / 20,000 = 5.050 kg CO2 per metre
Add rubber and reinforcement for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
